probe.question: I need to get the SNAr on our 2,4-dichloropyrimidine working with N-methylpiperazine — selectivity at the 4-position, 2 g of the pyrimidine, and we've banned DMF on this project. Write me a procedure I can actually run Thursday.
forbids_claims: a yield, conversion or selectivity ratio presented as something the record measured when no cited run reports it
a condition set drawn from general knowledge while the in-house record was not consulted
that the protocol has been reviewed, approved or scheduled by anyone
that DMF is acceptable here, or a solvent substitution made without saying it was substituted
probe.direction: The sentence contains four things — a transformation, a regiochemical objective, a scale and an exclusion — and a good answer structures that reading first and shows it, marking the 2 g and the DMF ban as the chemist's own words and anything it supplied (the vessel, the equivalents, the base) as its own inference. Named species are resolved rather than hand-written as SMILES. It then argues the conditions from what the record actually ran: whether this pyrimidine has been through an SNAr before, what base and solvent comparable displacements used and how often, and how the reagent was quenched — work-up is where a generated procedure is thinnest and where the technician notices first. What the record does not settle it computes or says it did not. The stored design comes back with an id and its checks, and the answer reports the warnings rather than suppressing them: a warning is a judgment for the chemist to make. Choosing a non-DMF solvent is required, and saying *which* constraint forced the swap is what makes it arguable. An answer that produces a plausible procedure with no citation behind any number is the failure here even when the chemistry is textbook-correct — the same reflex on a substrate with no textbook entry writes conditions out of nowhere.
